claims.claim: ring model has local symmetric E-E excitation and uniform global inhibition
neural firing is F(recurrent excitation + uniform inhibition), and recurrent excitation sums weighted presynaptic s_j
source-specific rate STP is coupled s,u,x ODE, with baseline U, tau_s, tau_u, tau_x and products u*x*phi
smaller U and longer tau_u produce greater facilitation effects in the authors' convention; U=1 corresponds to absent facilitation
source assumes continuous neutrally shifted stationary symmetric bump, large N and small fixed heterogeneity; other modes decay
Poisson spike count variability is replaced by mean/autocorrelation-matched Gaussian white noise for large network projection
near stationary bump, reduced center obeys dvarphi/dt = sqrt(B)*eta(t)+A(varphi) with ring periodic boundary
B is a source-defined spatially weighted sum of baseline rates with factors (C_i/S)^2*(dJ0i/dvarphi)^2; conventional Brownian D=B/2
drift field A(varphi) weighted sum of center-dependent first-order rate perturbations times C_i/S and input-profile derivative
source distinguishes fixed network-specific directional drift fields from zero ensemble-mean drift and location-invariant diffusion
very strong facilitation leaves nonzero residual drift/diffusion; vanishing facilitation plus increasing depression drives normalization toward zero at configuration-dependent critical tau_x
rate-model reduction via neutral translation mode uses left eigenvector; fast stable transverse dynamics assumed; multiplicative spike noise omitted at first order
spiking LIF comparison uses event-triggered STP with pre-spike efficacy/resources, one presynaptic spike train driving shared s,u,x updates; average steady-state rate gain is conditional
fixed heterogeneity variants are sparse Bernoulli E-E recurrent connections and Gaussian-distributed excitatory leak potentials, analyzed by first-order rate response
simulation comparisons report facilitation decreases diffusion and field magnitude while longer depression increases both over tested stable regimes
approximation underestimates/overestimates particular conditions: high heterogeneity over-predicts drift; strong facilitation may over-predict diffusion due to altered spiking irregularity
initial/final circular center distributions over 6.5s generate normalized mutual information; reduced and spiking predictions compared separately
weak external distractor enters as firing-rate perturbation inducing drift, predicting 250ms displacement only while bump shape is approximately fixed
system-size extrapolation starts from spiking-reference N_E=800, applies distinct size scaling for fast vs frozen noise and biological parameter estimates; is proof of principle
bump-loss trials excluded before estimates, especially weak facilitation/strong depression; finite ring diffusion cannot grow unbounded

simulated attractor circuit is not shown by this paper to be the biological cortical mechanism; unmodeled noisy STP, heterogeneity, adaptation, inhibitory topology and upstream/downstream noise remain
theoretical validation is against original spiking computational simulations and reduced Langevin comparisons, not exact direct behavioral empirical validation
source has reported Fig2 right-panel parameter inconsistency: main text and panel labels U=0.1 versus one sentence of Fig2B caption U=0.01; do not infer exact value from caption alone

material_limits.condition: without depression in this particular tuned setup bump was not stable at low rate; tau_x kept positive
networks deliberately retuned to obtain near-identical bump shapes across STP settings
stationary bump, N large, weak heterogeneity, Poisson-to-Gaussian proxy are necessary for reduction
strong facilitation leaves residual noise and drift, not perfect stabilization
without facilitation depression can approach configuration-dependent instability and divergent prediction near tau_x critical; quoted critical value pertains to chosen reference
short tau_s bump stability and full theory validity not tested in spiking simulations
large heterogeneity beyond first-order expansion overpredicts drift; steep drift trajectories numerically undersampled
low U suppresses irregularity of high-rate neurons and Poisson approximation can overpredict diffusion
expected displacement approximation does not collapse relative MI uniformly at strong depression/weak facilitation
distractor approximation assumes weak external input and nearly unchanged bump shape; behavioral link only proof of principle
initial transient diffusion excluded by steady-state assumption; no observed constant-velocity traveling bump mode in this particular spiking model
additional noisy STP, recurrent weight noise, intrinsic adaptations, biological external input/output noise and distance-dependent inhibitory plasticity not included
steady-state spiking-rate approximation neglects correlations and approximately factorizes u and x
different random recurrent and leak-heterogeneity system-size scaling; p-reciprocity approximation only matches average connection probability
bump-loss repeats are omitted: text reports 222/1000 at U1 tau_x150, at most 15/1000 at U<=0.8 other settings, 250/1000 at U0.8 tau_x200
circular domain saturates mean-square displacement; diffusion slope fit has finite time/window/initial transient exclusions
